questions.stem: An element is in Group 2 of the periodic table. What charge ion will it most likely form?

options.text: It will not form an ion

questions.explanation: Group 2 elements have 2 electrons in their outer shell. They lose these 2 electrons to achieve a stable full outer shell, forming 2+ ions.

questions.stem: Element X is in Group 7 and Period 4. Which element has the most similar chemical properties to X?
questions.explanation: Elements in the same group have similar chemical properties because they have the same number of outer shell electrons. An element in Group 7, Period 3 would react most similarly.

questions.stem: Using trends, if an unknown element is between sodium and potassium in Group 1, what can you predict about its reactivity with water?

options.text: It would not react with water
It would be less reactive than sodium
It would be more reactive than sodium but less reactive than potassium
It would be more reactive than potassium

questions.explanation: Reactivity increases down Group 1. An element between sodium and potassium would be more reactive than sodium but less reactive than potassium, following the trend.

questions.stem: An element in Group 6 would be expected to form which type of bond with a metal?

options.text: An ionic bond, forming a 2- ion

questions.explanation: Group 6 elements have 6 outer electrons and need to gain 2 more to fill their outer shell. When bonding with metals, they gain 2 electrons to form 2- ions in ionic compounds.

questions.stem: Based on the periodic table, which element would have the highest melting point: Na, Mg, or Al?

options.text: They would all have the same melting point

questions.explanation: Across Period 3, metallic bonding strength increases because the ions have a greater charge and there are more delocalised electrons. Aluminium (3+) has stronger metallic bonding than magnesium (2+) or sodium (1+).

questions.stem: What would be the formula of a compound formed between an element in Group 1 and an element in Group 7?
questions.explanation: A Group 1 element forms 1+ ions and a Group 7 element forms 1- ions. One of each combines to balance the charges, giving the formula XY (e.g., NaCl).

questions.stem: Astatine is at the bottom of Group 7. Based on the trends, which prediction is correct?

options.text: It would be a gas at room temperature
It would be more reactive than fluorine
It would be a solid at room temperature and less reactive than iodine

questions.explanation: Following the trends in Group 7: melting/boiling points increase down the group (so astatine would be solid) and reactivity decreases (so astatine would be less reactive than iodine).
